text.p: Stolt-Nielsen SA said on Tuesday it would increasingly operate its core chemical transportation divisions in concert to provide integrated services.

Chairman Jacob Stolt-Nielsen told a London shareholders meeting: "We have been used to thinking in terms of three separate business streams. But we have seen the synergy between the three and are now thinking in terms of one business line."

The group operates the world's largest chemical parcel tanker fleet within the Stolt Parcel Tankers division, transports chemical containers within its Stolt Tank Containers division and has a terminal operating arm in Stolthaven Terminals.
Stolt-Nielsen said the group had developed supplier partnerships and strategic alliances with 14 global chemical producers.

Stolt Tank Containers managing director Reginald Lee said: "I can see a time when Stolt Parcel Tankers are moving the bulk cargoes around the world and Tank Containers are making the regional movements."
"To date we have just scratched the surface with Tank Containers. This can go on building for 10 years but we already he have a world-wide network whereas most others are only regional," he said.
Lee said: "We are trying to get our customers to realise it is easier to put chemicals into tank containers" adding that they could be used for ship, rail and road movements.
Stolt-Nielsen added that the group would also continue to expand its terminal operations for operational reasons.
"We will see an increase in our engagement in terminals despite not getting such as impressive a return on capital from them. The benefits come in terms of our transport operations," he said.

The group said it was exploring expansion opportunities particularly in the fast growing Asia Pacific and South American markets. Stolthaven currently has three terminals in the U.S. and one in Brazil.

Stolt Parcel Tankers is engaged in a fleet renewal programme which will have seen it take delivery of 21 new ships between 1996 and the end of 1999. Stolt-Nielsen said it would scrap 13 vessels over the same period. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
